# Qeetrix (@qeetrix/ui)

> Qeetrix is Qeet Group's shared design system: one published npm package
> (`@qeetrix/ui`) of 145 accessible, token-driven React components built on
> Base UI + Tailwind v4, with W3C-DTCG design tokens (OKLCH, WCAG-AA gated) and a
> Qeet-orange brand. It powers Qeet ID, qeet-docs, qeet-notify and qeet-logs.

## Install

- `bun add @qeetrix/ui react react-dom`
- Import the stylesheet once: `@import "@qeetrix/ui/styles.css";`
- Import components from the barrel: `import { Button, Card } from "@qeetrix/ui";`
- Light/dark via the `.dark` class (managed by `ThemeProvider`).

## Import surfaces

- `@qeetrix/ui` — components, blocks re-exports, hooks, `cn`
- `@qeetrix/ui/styles.css` — tokens + fonts + base layer (side-effect import)
- `@qeetrix/ui/tokens.css` — raw `--qx-*` custom properties · `@qeetrix/ui/tokens.json`
- `@qeetrix/ui/brand` — QeetLogo + brand icons · `@qeetrix/ui/blocks` — composed patterns

## Design tokens (~451 per theme)

Authored as W3C DTCG JSON (`packages/qeetrix-ui/tokens/**`), compiled by Style Dictionary to
CSS custom properties (`--qx-*`) + JSON. Colour is OKLCH; every required text/surface
pair is held to WCAG-AA by a build gate. Brand = Qeet orange (`#F26D0E`). A Tokens
Studio / Figma export lives at `packages/qeetrix-ui/tokens-studio/`.

# Full context


## Guide: Accessibility

import { Meta } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

<Meta title="Guides/Accessibility" />

# Accessibility

Qeetrix targets **WCAG 2.1 AA** and **EN 301 549**, built on Base UI (WAI-ARIA APG
behaviour). Accessibility is enforced, not aspirational.

## What's guaranteed

- **Keyboard + ARIA** — interactive components inherit APG keyboard models, focus
  management, and roles/states from Base UI.
- **Contrast** — every required text/surface pair is held to AA by a token-level gate
  (`bun run tokens:validate`); the Qeet-orange brand pairs are enforced too.
- **Visible focus**, reduced-motion support, light/dark, and RTL throughout.

## Automated coverage

- `bun run --filter @qeetrix/ui test` runs Vitest + `vitest-axe`.
- `bun run --filter @qeetrix/ui test:a11y-coverage` is a **ratchet**: every component must
  have an automated a11y test, be in the smoke harness, or be on a shrinking exemption
  list. CI enforces it.

## For contributors

Run the per-component review in `docs/accessibility/audit-checklist.md` before shipping.
The conformance report template lives in `docs/accessibility/VPAT.md` (currently
self-reported, pending a third-party audit).

## Known caveat

`text.link` on white is currently ~3:1 with the orange brand — fine for large/UI text
but below the 4.5:1 body-text bar. Prefer `Button`/`Typography` link styling in dense
body copy until this is resolved (tracked in ADR 0004).


## Guide: Design Tokens

import { Meta } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

<Meta title="Guides/Design Tokens" />

# Design tokens

Tokens are the single source of truth. Everything downstream (components, themes, the
Figma export) is generated or composed from them.

## Pipeline

W3C **DTCG JSON** (`packages/ui/tokens/**`) → **Style Dictionary**
(`scripts/build-tokens.mjs`) → generated CSS + JSON. Three layers:

- **primitive** — raw ramps (OKLCH colour, spacing, radius, shadow, motion, …)
- **semantic** — meaning (`text.primary`, `surface.canvas`, `action.primary`, …), per theme
- **bridge** — the shadcn/Base-UI variables (`--primary`, `--ring`, …), per theme

## Consuming tokens

- `@qeetrix/ui/styles.css` — the semantic `:root` / `.dark` variables, baked in
- `@qeetrix/ui/tokens.css` — the raw `--qx-*` ramp
- `@qeetrix/ui/tokens.json` — resolved values per theme (cross-platform)

```css
.badge { background: var(--qx-color-brand-500); }
.hero  { background: var(--qx-gradient-brand); } /* composite gradient token */
```

## Guarantees

- Colour is authored in **OKLCH**.
- A **WCAG-AA contrast gate** (`bun run tokens:validate`) fails the build if a required
  text/surface pair drops below AA.
- **Composite tokens** (`gradient`, `strokeStyle`) serialize to real CSS
  (`linear-gradient(…)`, `dashed`) — see `--qx-gradient-*` / `--qx-stroke-*`.

## Figma / Tokens Studio

`bun run --filter @qeetrix/ui tokens:studio` exports the tokens into
`packages/ui/tokens-studio/` (DTCG sets + `$themes.json`/`$metadata.json`) for the
Tokens Studio Figma plugin to import as Variables.


## Guide: Foundation Modes

import { Meta } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

<Meta title="Guides/Foundation modes" />

# Foundation modes

Qeetrix keeps language, direction, density, color theme, motion preference, and viewport behavior
as separate concerns. Compose only the modes an application owns.

## Language and direction

`I18nProvider` supplies system-owned component strings and sets the document `lang` by default.
Set `setDocumentLanguage={false}` when the host already owns that attribute. Language does not
imply direction; compose `DirectionProvider` explicitly for RTL layouts.

```tsx
<I18nProvider locale="ar" messages={ar}>
  <DirectionProvider direction="rtl">{children}</DirectionProvider>
</I18nProvider>
```

Caller-owned content, option labels, and product terminology remain the caller's responsibility.

## Density

Density is opt-in so existing consumers retain their current dimensions. Use a subtree for a
preview or embedded tool, or apply the mode to the document at the app root.

```tsx
<DensityProvider density="compact" scope="document">
  {children}
</DensityProvider>
```

Default-sized controls, field rhythm, and table cells consume the generated density variables.
Explicit `xs`, `sm`, and `lg` sizes remain explicit overrides. Density never replaces mobile touch
guidance; use comfortable density for coarse-pointer primary workflows.

## Forced colors and focus

`styles.css` maps semantic colors to browser system colors under `forced-colors: active`. Focused
elements receive a token-driven `Highlight` outline even when shadows and custom rings are removed.
Do not disable `forced-color-adjust` on interactive controls without a tested reason.

## Responsive behavior

Use CSS first. `Container` provides the standard centered shell and responsive gutters. Tailwind's
default `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, and `2xl` ladder is canonical. `useMediaQuery`, `useIsMobile`, and
the exported query helpers are for behavioral adaptation only, such as switching a split view to a
modal detail panel.

## Token layers and enforcement

Primitive values feed semantic light/dark roles, stable component metrics, shared interaction
state, and data-visualization roles. `build-tokens` generates runtime CSS and typed values from the
same DTCG source; do not mirror motion, icon, stacking, shadow, or component constants by hand.

Use `--chart-1` through `--chart-8` for categorical identity and the dedicated grid, axis,
reference, positive, negative, and warning roles for chart structure and meaning. Run
`bun run tokens:scan` before review; exemptions are limited to documented domain data and
third-party selector shims.

## Guide: Getting Started

import { Meta } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

<Meta title="Guides/Getting Started" />

# Getting started

Qeetrix ships as a single package — components, tokens, and brand assets are all in
`@qeetrix/ui`.

## Install

```bash
bun add @qeetrix/ui react react-dom
```

## Wire up styles (Tailwind v4)

In your global stylesheet, import the Qeetrix layer once, and let Tailwind see the
component classes:

```css
@import "@qeetrix/ui/styles.css";
@source "../node_modules/@qeetrix/ui/dist/**/*.js";
```

## Use it

```tsx
import { ThemeProvider, Button, Card, CardContent } from "@qeetrix/ui";
import { QeetLogo } from "@qeetrix/ui/brand";

export function App() {
  return (
    <ThemeProvider defaultTheme="system">
      <Card>
        <CardContent className="flex items-center gap-3">
          <QeetLogo size={28} />
          <Button>Authenticate with Qeet</Button>
        </CardContent>
      </Card>
    </ThemeProvider>
  );
}
```

Light and dark are driven by the `.dark` class, which `ThemeProvider` manages. RTL is
handled by `DirectionProvider`.

## Import surfaces

- `@qeetrix/ui` — the barrel (components, hooks, `cn`)
- `@qeetrix/ui/styles.css` — tokens + fonts + base layer
- `@qeetrix/ui/brand` — `QeetLogo` + brand icons
- `@qeetrix/ui/blocks` — composed multi-component patterns (auth, dashboard shell, …)
- `@qeetrix/ui/tokens.css` / `@qeetrix/ui/tokens.json` — raw design tokens

See **Theming** and **Design tokens** for customisation.


## Guide: Theming

import { Meta } from "@storybook/addon-docs/blocks";

<Meta title="Guides/Theming" />

# Theming

Qeetrix is themed entirely through semantic CSS custom properties. Components never
hard-code colour — they read tokens — so theming is a matter of overriding variables.

## Light and dark

Both themes ship in `@qeetrix/ui/styles.css`. Toggle by adding/removing the `.dark`
class on a root element; `ThemeProvider` does this for you (`system` | `light` | `dark`).

```tsx
import { ThemeProvider } from "@qeetrix/ui";
<ThemeProvider defaultTheme="system">{children}</ThemeProvider>;
```

## Brand colour

The brand is **Qeet orange** (`#F26D0E` ≈ `orange.500`). Primary buttons, links, focus
rings and the shadcn `--primary` / `--ring` bridge resolve to the brand ramp, with a
dark on-brand foreground for AA contrast. To re-brand, re-point the `color.brand.*`
aliases in `packages/ui/tokens/primitive/color.json` — semantic and component layers
need no change (see ADR 0004).

## Overriding tokens in a consuming app

Import the Qeetrix layer, then override the variables you want *after* it:

```css
@import "@qeetrix/ui/styles.css";

:root {
  /* nudge the accent surfaces without touching the package */
  --primary: oklch(0.62 0.20 250); /* your blue */
}
```

Prefer overriding the **semantic** bridge variables (`--primary`, `--ring`, `--muted`, …)
rather than raw `--qx-*` primitives, so light/dark and future ramps stay coherent.

## RTL

Wrap in `DirectionProvider` (`direction="rtl"`) — logical properties and the
`rtl:` variants in components flip automatically.


## CONTRIBUTING.md

# Contributing to Qeetrix

## Setup

```bash
bun install
bun run build
```

Node ≥ 20, Bun ≥ 1.3 (the sole package manager — `bun@>=1.3` in `engines`).

## Add or change a token

Tokens live in [`packages/ui/tokens`](packages/ui/tokens) as W3C Design Tokens JSON
(`primitive/` → `theme/{light,dark}/{semantic,bridge}.json`). Edit those, then:

```bash
bun run --filter @qeetrix/ui build-tokens      # regenerates src/styles/tokens.{css,raw.css,json}
bun run --filter @qeetrix/ui validate-tokens   # WCAG-AA contrast guard
```

- The neutral, status, and **brand** ramps are real. Brand is **Qeet orange** (`#F26D0E`,
  OD-DS-03 — see [docs/adr/0004](docs/adr/0004-brand-color-od-ds-03.md)); the `accent` and
  `passkey` sub-ramps are still neutral placeholders. Re-brand by re-pointing only the primitive
  ramps in `primitive/color.json` — semantic, bridge and component layers are untouched.
- Never hand-edit `:root` / `.dark` in `@qeetrix/ui` — those come from the generated `src/styles/tokens.css`.

## Add a component

```bash
cd packages/ui
npx shadcn@latest add <component>   # drops Base UI variants into src/components/ui
```

Then export it from `src/index.ts`, build (`bun run --filter @qeetrix/ui build`), and add a story in
`apps/qeetrix-story/stories/primitives/<component>.stories.tsx` importing from `@qeetrix/ui`.

- Components must stay **Base UI only** (no Radix). Client components keep their `"use client"`
  directive — the `tsc` build preserves it.

## Quality gates

```bash
bunx turbo run lint typecheck build
bun run --filter @qeetrix/ui test              # Vitest + axe (also runs in CI)
bun run --filter @qeetrix/ui validate-tokens
bun run --filter @qeetrix/docs build-storybook
```

## Releasing

Record a changeset with every user-facing change:

```bash
bun run changeset
```

Commit the generated file. Merging to `main` opens a **Version Packages** PR; merging that
publishes the changed public packages to npm. See [.changeset/README.md](.changeset/README.md).

## Decisions (ADRs)

Significant, hard-to-reverse choices are recorded in [`docs/adr/`](docs/adr/) (single-package
strategy, Base UI, the token pipeline, the brand color, releases). Read them before proposing an
architectural change; to revisit a past decision, add a *new* ADR that supersedes it rather than
rewriting the old one.
